output.title: Check the process before you automate it
output.body:
Before you build a regression suite around a workflow, first ask whether the workflow is stable enough to deserve one. For a small business owner, that usually means one repeatable task: customer questions, invoices, or data work. The question is simple: does this task produce the same kind of output most times, or do people quietly handle exceptions in different ways each week?

If the manual process is already inconsistent, automation will not fix that. It will just repeat the inconsistency faster. The useful boundary is not “can AI do this?” but “can I describe this process clearly enough that someone else would follow the same steps and get the same result?”

A practical next step is to document one workflow on a single page: trigger, inputs, steps, edge cases, and the point where a human must still check the work. That gives you a real basis for deciding whether to keep it manual, standardise it first, or automate part of it later. Bareni’s diagnostic approach starts with the same discipline: identify one recurring workflow and be honest about whether it is ready for automation. Then write down where it breaks.
